text:
maria: Hey team — customers reporting sudden cross-region latency + auth 401s since policy change ~11:45 UTC. Looks like a bunch of requests are landing in eu-west-1 instead of us-east-1, spike in egress billing. Any idea what changed?
sam: saw the same alerts. CS getting multiple reports: 500ms -> 2s p95, some 401s for API keys that normally work.
leo: checking routing service logs now. Can anyone point to the policy commit id?
maria: @sam pasted the commit link in the ticket: https://console.redwood.internal/policies/commit/ci-8729 
sam: commit shows change to project: "svc-checkout" failover policy. tiny edit in priorities.
jordan: dug into the commit diff — looks innocuous, just reordered priorities. But the JSON in the commit is weird: the priority list is missing the first entry, looks truncated.
ops-kate: if the priority array got truncated the fallback order could default to region list order (eu first for this customer). That would explain cross-region hits.
leo: uploading a snippet of routing log: ```routing.eval ts=2026-03-16T11:46:02Z req_id=abc123 selected_region=eu-west-1 reason=policy_fallback priority_index=0```
maria: customers are seeing 401s too — could that be token audience mismatch for eu nodes?
jordan: yes — tokens issued scoped to us-east-1 cluster. Hitting eu nodes returns 401 from auth proxy.
deploy-bot: deploy event: policy-service:commit=ci-8729 applied to prod at 2026-03-16T11:45:55Z by web-ui
sam: urgent repro steps I used: 1) call /v1/generate with api-key X (bound to us-east), 2) watch headers X-Region-Hit, 3) observe 401 and higher latency.
leo: quick check in gitops manifest shows YAML loader replaced a JSON array with a single-line string when anchor expansion occurred. Example bad content: ```failover_priorities: "[\"eu-west-1\", \"us-east-1\"]"``` expected a list but got a string so our validator coerced it and truncated to first token during policy compile.
ops-kate: that explains the truncated array -> priority_index=0 pointing to EU. Oof.
maria: rolling back immediately? Which quick mitigation gets customers back to us-east?
jordan: short-term: force route override for the affected api-key(s) to us-east via routing console (per-key affinity override). I'll push patch to routing-service to ignore stringified arrays while we fix pipeline.
leo: rolling rollback of commit ci-8729 now. Deploy-bot should show status.
deploy-bot: rollback event: policy-service:rollback=ci-8728 initiated by leo at 2026-03-16T11:52:10Z
sam: CS confirmed a subset of customers are recovering after rollback, latencies dropping. Still seeing a handful of 401s — tokens may need revalidation TTL.
jordan: action items: 1) patch gitops YAML -> ensure arrays preserved (assigned: eng-infra/leo), 2) add validation in policy-service to reject stringified arrays (assigned: eng/ops-kate), 3) backfill alert to detect sudden region shift per-key (assigned: eng-sre/jordan), 4) contact billing to review egress spike (assigned: finance).
ops-kate: created ticket INFRA-2314 with repro, logs, and temp ACL change instructions.
maria: any ETA on patch for validator?
jordan: can get a hotfix out in ~2hrs, but I'll push a config rule now to reject policies where priorities aren't a real list which should prevent further bad commits.
leo: note for postmortem — this only happened when policies were edited via the web UI with a YAML import from our gitops flow that relies on anchors. Manual edits probably ok. Add test for anchor-preserving serializer.
sam: customer-facing update drafted: "We experienced a configuration issue that temporarily routed some traffic to EU nodes causing higher latency and authentication failures for keys scoped to US clusters. We rolled back the policy and are monitoring. Investigating root cause and will follow up." cc @maria
maria: thanks everyone. I'll escalate to account execs for affected customers and attach the ticket. Please ping here when validator fix is live. :thumbsup:
